a previously unrecognized function of ANP proteins in intracellular signaling in response to elicitor perception.

the N-terminal region of ANPs is required for the elicitor-induced intracellular ROS accumulation.
ANPs are required for the intracellular ROS accumulation that occurs in the multiple organelles after elicitor treatment and that this process requires their localization in the multiple organnelles.
ANPs are involved in the elicitor-triggered ROS accumulation in the cytosolic, plastidial and nuclear compartments, which in turn is required for the activation of immune responses in Arabidopsis.

the intracellular ROS accumulation requires the multiple organellar-targeted NPK1-related Arabidopsis protein kinases.
the ANP protein kinases are required for ROS accumulation and that the localization of the ANPs coincides spatially with the sites of ROS accumulation.
the intracellular ROS accumulation is an early event of the plant immune response and that it requires the multiple organellar targeted ANP kinases.

the intracellular ROS accumulation requires the multiple organellar targeted ANP1-ANP3.
the NPK1-related kinases are localized in the mitochondria and the chloroplasts and that they are required for the accumulation of ROS in the organelles.
